title: Man shot after threatening RCMP with table leg
article: Penticton RCMP expect assault charges to be approved today against a man they shot in the stomach after he threatened two officers with a broken stick of furniture.
Police were called to an apartment complex on Saturday where they confronted a 34-year-old man with a history of mental illness. They say the man threatened them and tried to slam the door on them.

When the two officers forced their way into the apartment suite, the man began "throwing just about anything he could get his hands on at the officers," Penticton RCMP Corporal Rick Dellebuur said in an interview yesterday.
The man then snapped a leg off a television stand and brandished it as a weapon. He was pepper-sprayed without effect and ignored repeated warnings to drop the stick or be shot.

When he took a swing at one of the officers, he was shot in the abdomen once with a 9 mm handgun. The man was treated in hospital before being transferred to police cells yesterday morning to await charges.

Although the Penticton RCMP detachment does use tasers, not all members of the force are trained in their use and there are not enough units for every member. The two officers at the scene were not armed with the stun gun at the time.

The use of tasers in policing is currently the subject of an inquiry since the death of Robert Dziekanski last fall. The disoriented Polish immigrant was shot twice with a taser at the Vancouver International Airport before he died.
The conduct of the Penticton police in the weekend shooting will be investigated by the provincial arm of the RCMP in a standard review into the use of force.
"A leg from a piece of furniture is just like a baseball bat, it could cause grievous harm depending on how it is used," Cpl. Dellebuur said.
He said the officer who shot the man will have to justify his actions in the police review of the incident.
Cpl. Dellebuur said the man was known to police and was believed to have been under the influence of alcohol.

The two officers were both experienced. One was a regular member with at least six years on the force, the other was a reserve member. Reserve members are drawn from the ranks of retired officers and typically have two decades of experience, he said.

Penticton RCMP were already preparing to be in the spotlight this week as an inquest begins in Vancouver into the death of Steven Qualtier. Mr. Qualtier was found dead in a Penticton RCMP cell on Aug. 5, 2007. He had been arrested the day before in the nearby Okanagan town of Keremeos.
